doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: From LPs to CDs and live vocals with a band
summary: Hank says the move to CDs should not change the recording, and discusses singers doing live vocals with a rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: How about the final product? When we moved from LPs to CDs did it change necessarily the way you recorded things and the final product?

It better not. I mean if you’re working with a vocalist let’s say and you get a nice mix, you’re going to have that mix all the way. You know? You can’t suddenly change unless like you do a vocal with a rhythm section and you know they’re going to add strings or horns or something like that. Then that’s a different ballgame. The artist has to make sure that he just does his vocal. You know he has to disfranchise himself from a band. He’s working with a rhythm section. It’s kind of different. Some work very well that way. There were some acts that just sang better, felt better doing live vocals with a band. You know? Very few though, I must say.
